record.summary: Presidential memorandum on AI and national security, with a classified annex. Its three objectives: lead the world's development of safe, secure and trustworthy AI; harness AI with safeguards for national security; and cultivate a stable, responsible framework for international AI governance. It makes the AI Safety Institute the government's primary point of contact with AI developers for voluntary pre- and post-deployment testing of frontier models, including for cyber and biological and chemical weapons risks, and requires a Framework to Advance AI Governance and Risk Management in National Security setting prohibited and high-impact AI uses with minimum risk management practices.
record.notes: Signed by President Biden on 24 Oct 2024. It fulfils the directive in subsection 4.8 of his executive order on AI (EO 14110, US-04). The companion Framework to Advance AI Governance and Risk Management in National Security was published the same day; the memorandum has the NSC Deputies Committee approve the Framework and review it periodically. The White House fact sheet of the same day also says the memorandum makes collection on competitors' operations against the US AI sector a top-tier intelligence priority; the memorandum's public text directs a review of the intelligence priorities to improve the identification of foreign intelligence threats to the US AI ecosystem. NSPM-11 of 5 Jun 2026 (US-28), section 3(f), rescinds and replaces NSM-25 and associated guidance.

legal_force.quote: Commerce, acting through the AI Safety Institute (AISI) within the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), shall serve as the primary United States Government point of contact with private sector AI developers
This memorandum shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.

summary.quote: A classified annex to this memorandum addresses additional sensitive national security issues
(a) First, the United States must lead the world’s development of safe, secure, and trustworthy AI.
(b) Second, the United States Government must harness powerful AI, with appropriate safeguards, to achieve national security objectives.
(c) Third, the United States Government must continue cultivating a stable and responsible framework to advance international AI governance

shall serve as the primary United States Government point of contact with private sector AI developers to facilitate voluntary pre- and post-public deployment testing for safety, security, and trustworthiness of frontier AI models.
This testing shall assess models’ capabilities to aid offensive cyber operations, accelerate development of biological and/or chemical weapons, autonomously carry out malicious behavior
(C) Guidance on AI activities that pose unacceptable levels of risk and that shall be prohibited.
(D) Guidance on AI activities that are “high impact” and require minimum risk management practices

notes.quote: This memorandum fulfills the directive set forth in subsection 4.8 of Executive Order 14110 of October 30, 2023
The AI Framework shall be approved by the NSC Deputies Committee
and shall be reviewed periodically through that process
